body.rationale: The IPS (config/ips.yaml) is still a draft, so I treated the breach counts as provisional evidence. I favoured portfolios that are IPS-clean or close to it and that rely on covariance or tail structure more than on fragile return forecasts, in line with the late-cycle finding in §4.3. 1) black_litterman: no hard breaches, the shallowest drawdown of the three clean return-optimised books (-21.2%), a CRO score of 0.40, 6.1 effective assets, and a backtest Sharpe of 0.70. Its reviewer confirmed the numbers reconcile and noted that it discloses the gamma tuning. The main risk is sitting on the 8% volatility boundary, which is a draft-IPS sensitivity and not a method error. 2) cvar_minimization: no breaches, a -18.7% drawdown, and the best backtest Sharpe (0.74). It uses actual tail scenarios, which suits a late-cycle regime. Its weaknesses are the 2.9 effective assets and that its tail hedges are fitted to a handful of crises. 3) resampled_efficient_frontier: no breaches and diffuse (13.3 effective assets). Its reviewers found no flaw in the numbers, and the one technical error, the gamma description, is about wording and not about the weights. It ranks third because the drawdown headroom is under 1 point (-24.3% vs -25%) and resampling cannot remove a common CMA bias. 4) tail_risk_parity: it adds a different family and a downside-risk lens, with 6.0 effective assets and a -7.2% drawdown. It does breach return, volatility and tracking error, which is why it is not higher. The reviewer's point that cash adds no excess return to its Sharpe is a framing issue, not a defect in the weights. 5) inverse_volatility: a diversified low-risk heuristic (7.6 effective assets, -9.0% drawdown, CRO 0.30). It is a useful defensive anchor, but it breaches three limits and puts about 46% in cash, so it is a tilt component and not a core book. The first choice beats the fifth because black_litterman passes every IPS limit with a 0.70 backtest Sharpe and a real return target, while inverse_volatility misses the return, volatility-band and tracking-error limits and depends on one near-zero cash sigma. I left out max_sharpe because 46% in us_value rests on one judged CMA gap, as its own reviewers noted. Flag: market_cap_weight, which has the worst drawdown (-40.6%), the highest CRO risk (0.80), and weights drawn from an ETF-AUM proxy that double-counts nested equity sleeves and has no meaningful size for gold, commodities or cash. Its reviewers called this a technical error, and the CIO should not lean on it.
